attr.alt: Dr. Nahlah — Implants and Prosthodontics Specialists
Dr. Esam Nahlah with a patient

nodes.v: Board-certified prosthodontist. Diplomate of the American Board of Prosthodontics. Hospital privileges at Inova Fairfax. Practising since 2003, in Northern Virginia since 2013.
Three more years, spent entirely on the hard cases.
Prosthodontics is one of twelve dental specialties recognised in the United States. It is the one concerned with
— implants, crowns, bridges, veneers, dentures and full-mouth rehabilitation — and it takes three years of training beyond dental school to practise.
Dr. Nahlah has been a practising dentist
. He moved to Northern Virginia in 2013 to focus entirely on prosthodontics: esthetic dentistry, implant dentistry, full-mouth rehabilitation and smile makeovers.
2013 the American Board of Prosthodontics awarded him Diplomate status
, the most prestigious credential in the field. He holds hospital privileges at
, the only Level 1 trauma hospital in Northern Virginia.

He has published in national and international scientific journals and lectures extensively on smile design and dental implants — the kind of work that tends to bring other dentists’ difficult cases to his door.
The home page shows eight of these. Here is the complete list as published by the practice.
M.S., Master of Science in Oral Biology
Fellow, International Congress of Oral Implantologists
Associate Fellow, American Academy of Implant Dentistry
CRDTS, Central Regional Dental Testing Service

attr.alt: A trophy — the practice's illustration for its award recognition

nodes.v: He teaches the dentists who refer to him.
clinical instructor at the University of California, San Francisco School of Dentistry
before relocating. He still takes time out of the practice to run hands-on courses and lectures for other dentists.
, a quarterly symposium — for dentists, by dentists — built to challenge how the profession thinks and to raise the standard of care its members deliver.
Techniques he brought in, and keeps current.
Implants placed at the time of extraction where the case allows, removing a healing phase and a separate surgery.
Placement through a surgical guide generated from the cone-beam scan, so each post lands at the planned angle and depth.
Scanned rather than moulded, which removes a step patients dislike and a source of dimensional error.
The half most surgeons hand off. Planning and restoring in the same practice is the reason the final teeth match the plan.

attr.alt: Dr. Nahlah with the practice team

nodes.v: The part that is not on a certificate.

Dr. Nahlah’s stated primary focus is practising dentistry and caring for patients. In his own words, what he does with the rest of it is spend time with his wife and family, ride motorcycles, hike, boat, and — more recently — cycle.
Two offices, one team, and a laboratory in the building. If you have been told your case is too complex, that combination is usually why it is not.
The specialty applied: what an implant is and how it is planned.
Six patients filmed at the practice.
Have the specialist look at it.
Consultations include the 3D scan and a straight answer — including second opinions on implant surgery, which are free.
Implant dentistry and prosthodontics for Northern Virginia — rebuilding smiles that other practices call too complex.
